thread:
incbot: Pager: high tail-latency + kv cache memory growth for text-gen clusters in us-west-2. Alerts: tail_latency_p95 > 5s, kv_cache_size rising > 80% of shard. Models impacted: qwen-large-mqa, mistral-v2-gqa, llama-2-13b.
aliya (oncall): acked. viewing dashboards now, assigning.
aliya (oncall): initial hypothesis: continuous-batching config recently rolled (rollout 02:34 UTC) + prefix-KV miss expansion on MQA paths.
prateek: pulling logs for qwen-large-mqa on host pool gpux-14. seeing prefix blowups, lots of unique prefix keys.
matthew: @prateek can you paste the hot paths?
prateek: logs snippet:
```
2026-03-15T02:38:12Z WARN kv_cache: miss_count=12458 key_len=1024 model=qwen-large-mqa shard=23
2026-03-15T02:38:13Z INFO cont_batcher: batch_size=64 latency_ms=2300 model=qwen-large-mqa
2026-03-15T02:38:14Z WARN kv_cache: growth_rate=1.9x/5m estimated_shard_fill=92%
```
gina: ops dashboard shows 12% request failures (502/504) for customers using embeddings+generation pipeline that pins qwen-mqa. We should page SRE/public-customer-facing if we hit SLAs.
aliya (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) emergency rollback of continuous-batching for MQA models, 2) temporary aggressive KV eviction policy on affected shards, 3) throttle large-prefix requests.
prateek: I can push a targeted config via control-plane patch. Suggest patching only qwen-large-mqa and mistral-v2-gqa to set continuous_batching=false and batch_max_tokens=256.
matthew: sounds good. please include safety: canary on 10% first.
prateek: preparing curl patch now:
```
curl -X POST "https://internal-controlplane.redwood/api/v1/runtime-config" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"selector": {"model": ["qwen-large-mqa","mistral-v2-gqa"]}, "overrides": {"batching": {"continuous": false, "batch_max_tokens": 256}, "kv_cache": {"eviction": "aggressive"}}}'
```
infra-bot: deploy request queued: id=deploy-8392 scope=runtime-config user=prateek
aliya (oncall): do the canary (10%) for 2m, then ramp if healthy. watch tail latency and error count.
prateek: canary applied 02:46 UTC to 10% traffic. metrics: p95 latency dropped from ~5.8s -> 2.1s for canary group within 30s. kv_shard_fill delta for canary hosts reversed.
gina: customer impact update: two enterprise customers reported timeouts in last hour (sr tickets created). CS notified.
matthew: while this reduces latency, continuous batching off increases token-cost per request. we should communicate ephemeral cost increase to CS.
aliya (oncall): agree. CS: send holding message to impacted customers, noting we're mitigating and will follow up with RCA.
prateek: after 3m canary looks stable. initiating ramp to 100% for those models. infra-bot: deploy apply started id=deploy-8392 step=promote
infra-bot: deploy succeed id=deploy-8392 time=02:51 UTC
aliya (oncall): rolling metrics: cluster-wide p95 down 40%, error rate down to baseline. kv_shard_fill growth slowed but still above normal on some older shards, scheduling background TTL compaction.
prateek: adding a temporary eviction policy command to affected hosts via SSH runner:
```
# worker-side: reduce KV retention for prefix-sized entries
sudo /opt/redwood/bin/kvctl set-eviction --shard 23 --policy aggressive --max-age 30m
```
matthew: noted. also found an MQA-specific edge where certain prompt patterns create very long effective prefixes causing cache explosion. we should add a prompt-length cap in the request normalization layer.
gina: opening follow-up ticket: "prompt-normalization: cap prefix len for MQA/GQA models" and assigning to devex + runtime.
aliya (oncall): handoff to night oncall @prateek: leave notes in oncall doc + add a short checklist:
- what we changed (continuous_batching=false for qwen-large-mqa, mistral-v2-gqa)
- deploy id=deploy-8392
- observed improvement numbers
- customers impacted and sr ids: SR-2026-77, SR-2026-79
- follow-ups: ttl compaction job, prompt-normalization ticket, evaluation of cost bump
prateek: leaving notes in #oncall-log and tagging infra-runbook.
aliya (oncall): final note: root cause likely a combination of continuous-batching rollout + unbounded MQA prefix growth with skewed request distribution. temporary mitigations good. full RCA will include: kernel-level tracing of kv key gen, deeper traffic analysis, and a safer batching rollout strategy (gradual per-shard).
matthew: +1 on per-shard rollouts. also suggest adding an automated isolate switch: if shard_fill>90% and tail_latency rising, auto-disable continuous batching for that shard.
infra-bot: scheduled TTL compaction job job_id=compaction-442 start=03:30 UTC
gina: CS updated customers: holding message sent, two SRs with priority elevated.
prateek: I'll monitor overnight and loop in runtime team tomorrow for RCA.
aliya (oncall): handing off to @prateek for night watch. thanks everyone. :heart:
prateek: taking over. will ping if anything flares.
incbot: Thread closed (incident status: mitigated).
